subject: South Aral Sea
note: Cited to a pinned Wikipedia revision (trusted_secondary): Aral Sea. Natural Earth's lake outlines are not dated; the scene captions say which year each number is about.

claims.text: Formerly the third-largest lake in the world (68,000 km2), the Aral Sea shrank from the 1960s after Soviet irrigation diverted its rivers.
In 1987, the lake split into two separate bodies of water: the North Aral Sea and the South Aral Sea.
By 2007, it had declined to 10% of its original size, splitting into four lakes.
Satellite images by NASA in August 2014 revealed that the eastern basin of the Aral Sea had completely dried up.
The Dike Kokaral dam (2005) helped the North Aral Sea recover; by 2013 there were enough fish for some fishing.
